messages:
niko: Hey team — newbie here. Quick local setup issue: I ran `docker compose up` and migrations fail with `psycopg2.OperationalError: password authentication failed for user \"redwood_dev\"`. I set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env.local per the onboarding guide, but DB logs show the user exists and the password is empty. Any idea why compose isn't using my .env.local?

eli: Welcome! Docker Compose only automatically reads a file named `.env` in the compose folder. If you use `.env.local` you need to explicitly pass it with `--env-file` or rename it to `.env`. Also note that env interpolation in the compose file happens at parse time, so changing files after the container is created won't update already-created containers/volumes.

pat: Another gotcha: if you used a pre-initialized named volume, Postgres won't re-run initialization that sets the password. So even if you fix the envfile, the DB inside the volume still has the old auth state. If you want a clean start: `docker compose down -v` then `docker compose --env-file .env.local up -d` to ensure env is used on first init.

niko: Ah that explains it. I had an existing `repo_db_data` named volume from trying different branches. I renamed .env.local to .env and did `docker compose down -v` then `docker compose up -d` and it worked. Migrations now connect. Thanks!

tanya: Quick extra: prefer not to rename files if you want to keep local overrides separate. We usually do `docker compose --env-file .env.local up -d` in onboarding docs. Also for iterating without nuking volumes you can exec into the DB and `ALTER USER redwood_dev WITH PASSWORD 'newpw';` but be careful in case migration expects a fresh DB.

eli: Small checklist for others hitting this: 1) Confirm which env file compose is reading (`docker compose config` will show interpolated values). 2) If using `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}` in compose, ensure it's defined in the env file compose reads. 3) If DB already initialized, either alter the user inside Postgres or remove the volume and recreate. 4) Check `docker compose logs -f db` for init-time messages like "database system is ready to accept connections" and initial SQL executed.

pat: And one more subtle one: some onboarding scripts put secrets in `.env.local` but the compose file references env vars via `env_file:` rather than top-level env interpolation. `env_file` is evaluated differently — if you list `env_file: - .env` in the service, compose will load that file into the container env but still reads `.env` for interpolation at parse time. Use `docker compose --env-file` to be explicit.

niko: Great tips. I also ran `docker compose config` as suggested and saw the password blank for the db service before I renamed the file — good debug trick. I'll add a note to my onboarding checklist. Thanks all! :tada:

devex-bot: Helpful internal docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/dev-setup/local-postgres (section "env files & init volumes"). If anyone wants, @pat or @eli can pair for 10m to walk through your setup. :robot_face:
